repo.description:
### Impact

The app name validation regex `(^[a-z0-9][^/:_A-Z]*$)` permits shell metacharacters including `;`, `$`, backticks, `|`, `&`, `()`, `>`, and `<`. When an authenticated user pushes to a git remote with a crafted app name (e.g., `a;id`), the name is embedded unquoted into a bash pre-receive hook script via an unquoted heredoc (`<<EOF` instead of `<<'EOF'`) in `fn-git-create-hook()` at `plugins/git/internal-functions:378`. On git push, bash interprets the semicolon as a command separator, executing arbitrary commands as the dokku user.

This security issue applies to all installations and can be exploited by any user that has been granted push access to a Dokku installation.

### Patches

- https://github.com/dokku/dokku/pull/8590
repo.summary: OS Command Injection via App Name in Git Pre-Receive Hook
